sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Nursing Care During the Fourth Stage of Labor
sources.text: During this stage, the nurse will closely monitor the birthing person’s vital signs, uterine tone, lochia, and recovery from any anesthesia for complications and encourage parent-newborn bonding and breast-feeding. The nurse will also assist the health-care provider during the repair of any lacerations. Lochia Monitor amount, color, and consistency every 15 minutes for the first hour, every 30 minutes for the second hour, every hour for the third and fourth hours The lochia will remain rubra in color, will not contain large clots, and will remain consistent or decreased in quantity. Perineum Monitor for edema, ecchymoses, and discomfort every 15 minutes for the first hour, every 30 minutes for the second hour, every hour for the third and fourth hours The perineum will remain free from infection. sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Physiologic Changes During the Postpartum Period
sources.text: The nurse assesses the vaginal bleeding (lochia) and notes it has slowed to normal. Clinical judgment used by the nurse in this patient scenario : The nurse assesses the postpartum person for possible causes of the increased vaginal bleeding. Uterus and Lochia During the first 24 to 48 hours, the uterus involutes, or shrinks, to the approximate level of the umbilicus. The uterus shrinks approximately 1 cm per day and is within the confines of the pelvis by day 10, as illustrated in Figure 20.5 . If the nurse notices the fundus is not firm, the nurse should massage the uterus, assess the lochia, and administer oxytocin ( Pitocin ) according to postpartum orders. Complete involution of the uterus to the prepregnant size occurs over approximately 6 weeks. The old tissue is sloughed off as part of the lochia.
